column1: # Known non-green outcomes in the `porffor-cli` test targets.
# This file is TRACKED and LOAD-BEARING. `tests/cli/known_failures.rs` pulls it
# in with `include_str!`, so deleting it, renaming it, or letting a `.gitignore`
# rule swallow it is a compile error at `cargo check --all-targets` rather than
# a silent regression.
# HAZARD, and the reason this file is `.tsv`: `.gitignore` line 3 is a bare
# `*.txt`. An earlier revision of this ledger was written as
# `known-failures.txt`, `git add -A` dropped it without a word, and the
# references in `README.md` and `docs/rust-rewrite/batch-workflow.md` outlived
# the file they pointed at for three batches. Before adding ANY tracked data
# file, run `git check-ignore -v <path>` and require exit status 1. `.tsv` is
# also this repository's existing convention for hand-maintained tables -- see
# `test262/backlog/ownership-map.tsv` and
# `test262/backlog/shortcut-allowlist.tsv`.
# A row here is a DECLARATION, not a skip. AGENTS.md bans permanent skip lists
# and silent expected failures, so every row carries an owner task and a reason,
# and the outcome is enforced by libtest itself rather than by anyone
# remembering to compare against a list:
#   fail / hang -> the named test carries `should_panic` with a NON-EMPTY
#                  `expected` substring. The suite goes RED if the test starts
#                  passing ("test did not panic as expected") and RED if it
#                  fails for a different reason (message mismatch). Both delta
#                  directions, no end-of-run machinery.
#   ignored     -> the named test carries an `ignore` attribute with a reason.
#                  `known_failures::every_ignored_test_is_declared` rejects any
#                  ignore attribute in these targets that has no row here, and
#                  any row here whose test is no longer ignored.
#   unfilled    -> a placeholder for a failure set nobody has measured yet. The
#                  test column must be exactly `UNFILLED`, and the expiry header
#                  below stops it from becoming permanent.
# The expiry header is compared against `CURRENT_BATCH` in
# `tests/cli/known_failures.rs`. When `CURRENT_BATCH` reaches the batch named
# there, any surviving `unfilled` row fails `ledger_is_well_formed`. Extending
# the deadline is possible but shows up as a diff on this line.
# unfilled-allowed-until: batch-8
# Columns, tab-separated, sorted ascending by (target, test) and unique on that
# pair. Every column must be non-empty and carry no leading or trailing space.
#   target      cargo test target: async_generator | cli | perf. Closed set;
#               adding `tests/<name>.rs` without extending `TestTarget` fails
#               the hygiene tests.
#   test        libtest name WITHIN that target. `cli` is the target name, not a
#               module, so its names are rooted at `tests/cli/main.rs` and carry
#               no `cli::` prefix -- `binary_data::run_...`, not
#               `cli::binary_data::run_...`, which as a libtest filter matches
#               nothing at all.
#   state       fail | hang | ignored | unfilled. Closed set, parsed into an
#               enum; anything else is a hard parse error.
#   owner_task  T<NN>, backed by a real `tasks/<NN>-*.md`. Checked.
#   reason      Why this outcome is expected. No tabs.
#   evidence    A path, or a path plus a symbol. Deliberately NOT a line number:
#               line numbers rot silently and this ledger already lost one file
#               to a silent rot. CHECKED: the first whitespace-separated token
#               must resolve under the repo root and must not start with
#               `target/`. A gitignored citation is unverifiable on anyone
#               else's checkout, which is the exact failure mode this ledger
#               exists to end -- and this column carried one.
# target
cli
column5: Rung 1c is 15 of 20 chunks and 422 of 611 executing tests at this head (the write lane counted 17/503; the integrator then invalidated string and functions, because batch 7's RE-RT lane changed porffor-aot-wasm/src/{data,expressions}.rs and a compiler change is invisible to a sidecar that only counts test sources), so the failing set for the remainder is still unknown. language is the one chunk that has never produced a verdict at any head in four batches: as a single 105-test libtest process it was OOM-SIGKILLed three times in batch 6 at t+1200 s after 66, 75 and 75 tests, with avail falling monotonically from 8.5 GiB to 1.14 GiB, and the three runner-level environment knobs were measured to be no lever (per-tier cache limits bound disk not RSS; PORFFOR_CPU_PERCENT is overridden inside run_chunk) while --test-threads below 3 is banned. Those are environment knobs only: the accumulation's actual mechanism is WASM_MODULE_MEMORY_CACHE_ENTRIES in porffor-engine/src/lib.rs, an LRU of fully compiled Wasmtime modules bounded by entry count (64) and by no byte ceiling, retained on the in-process path these tests take -- which is why the disk knobs did nothing. That mechanism is a HYPOTHESIS and the banked chunks refute the entry-count form of it: array banked at 84 in-process run tests over 77 distinct fixtures (mean 1945 B), which pins the 64-entry LRU at its cap, and typed_array banked at 58 over 48 fixtures (mean 2716 B), inside the same 53/62/62 band the fatal language runs reached -- both with larger sources than language's 33 fixtures at mean 1285 B. The 53/62/62 figures are themselves tests_done minus 13, i.e. over-counts that assume one fixture per test, and frontend_test262_subset's flat 5.55 GiB is a CHILD process's RSS (frontend_test262_subset.rs:123 is ProcessCommand::new) so it is not evidence about an in-process LRU at all. PORFFOR_MODULE_MEMORY_CACHE_ENTRIES now overrides it and bounding it by bytes is the standing follow-up, so the split is the lever this batch reached for rather than the only lever there is. Batch 7 therefore split tests/cli/language.rs into language 45 + language_errors 29 + language_numerics 31, taking the chunk set from 18 to 20 so the same 105 tests run as three separate processes; those three have banked nothing yet. All 105 were measured green at the batch-6 head, but by the UNION of a 75-test chunk attempt and a standalone 30-name tail, and a union is not the banked verdict this row's own text sets as the standard. regexp and date are separately stale: banked at 33 and 17 while tests/cli/regexp.rs and tests/cli/date.rs now declare 35 and 18, so the counts sidecar re-runs both. Eight chunks therefore execute on the next run, not three: the three language modules, string, functions, regexp, date, and known_failures, which run_chunk re-runs unconditionally because it holds the chunk/module partition check this split just changed. Recount at the integrated head with the exact-line awk is 620 test attributes, 8 spec-exec-oracle gated in frontend.rs and one heap ignore, hence 612 compiled and 611 executing; the compiled count is measured here rather than derived, because cargo test -p porffor-cli --test cli -- --list printed 612 tests at integration and 620 minus 8 independently agrees. The only declared non-pass outcome across the 422 is the T05 heap ignore, which already has its row. Deleting this row now would declare a complete expected-failure set over three chunks that have never run, so batch 7 bumps CURRENT_BATCH to 7 and extends this header to batch-8 in one patch, both visible one-line diffs. DELETE this row rather than filling it the moment language, language_errors and language_numerics all bank green: the surviving set is then empty, and the deadline check is not evaluated at all once no unfilled row exists.

column5: Wall-clock acceptance benchmark that intentionally fails until the runtime/program split lands. Before this ledger it was an expected failure with a reason but no owner, no expiry and no record anywhere -- exactly the shape AGENTS.md rules out. It stays ignored: it is a timing acceptance gate, not a correctness test.
